name: Bun (Bun.serve)
workload: the-benchmarker/web-frameworks fair-comparison HTTP echo/plaintext workload at 512 concurrent connections
claimed_speedup: 145,896.6 rps (Bun) vs 67,239.1 rps (Go net/http stdlib) at 512 connections, ~2.17x (derived from page data)
hardware: M1 Eight-Core Processor per data.json hardware.cpu_name (note: os.machine field in same record says x86_64, an internal inconsistency in the suite's metadata; treat CPU identity with caution)
tradeoffs: Bun statically links LGPL-2 licensed JavaScriptCore/WebKit; caveat noted for LGPL relinking obligations. Not a drop-in for Go net/http (different language/runtime), uses io_uring/kqueue-backed Zig HTTP server under the hood, not a C++ library usable from C++ directly.
caveats: Benchmark is a third-party multi-language suite (the-benchmarker/web-frameworks), not a blog post with its own methodology write-up; per-framework compiler/build flags live in each framework's own Dockerfile in that repo rather than in the top-level data.json, so flags are not confirmed here. Hardware record has an internal inconsistency (cpu_name vs os.machine).
found_via: Blogs/talks task fallback: the-benchmarker/web-frameworks data.json (shared benchmark resource), go-language ranking sorted by total_requests_per_s at level 512, compared to nethttp baseline entry
